solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Laurel, Tom and Dick in conversation being crude

indicators.note: words spoken in conversation are heard rather than read, so the sound of the pieces counts

parts.note: the bay is a laurel tree; Cockney rhyming slang: Tom and Dick means sick

explanation.surface: Three named characters chatting crudely, as if Laurel of Laurel and Hardy joined two friends.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM AND DICK is Cockney rhyming slang for sick. BAY + SICK spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude and rudimentary both describe something simple and unrefined.

clue.text: Movement of sportsperson helps side

parts.note: to back someone is to help or support them
a wing is a side of a building or of a team's formation

explanation.surface: A sportsperson's movement helps their side.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's or batter's drawing back of the club or bat before striking is a movement of a sportsperson.

clue.text: Quick to grab a shower

indicators.note: one piece grabs the other, holding it within its letters

parts.note: spry means nimble or quick

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to snatch a quick shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray is a fine shower of liquid droplets.

clue.text: People study tailless bird

indicators.note: without its tail means the final letter of the word for study is dropped

parts.note: to check something is to study or examine it
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A field note: people studying a bird that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chechens are the people of Chechnya in the North Caucasus.

clue.text: Home ground unfinished, with little space originally to house footballers

indicators.note: one piece houses another, holding it inside
originally means at the start, so the little space comes before the ground word

parts.note: an en is a printer's small unit of space

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: milled means ground, as grain is in a mill
the FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: A home ground left incomplete, with a little space set aside for the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' says the little space comes first, before the ground word; 'to house' then puts the footballers between the two. The French phrase is used in English.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase describes being at home with one's family, informally and privately.

clue.text: Article replaced by European in living area

indicators.note: one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

parts.note: extant means still living or in existence
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item in a living room is swapped for a European one.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the size or area covered by something.

clue.text: Reservation to get table at front, upon hearing critic's remarks

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits upon the next, above it

parts.note: for can mean in order to get, as in 'go for gold'

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
on hearing means the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: knocks are a critic's disparaging remarks

explanation.surface: Booking a front table at a restaurant after hearing what the critic said.
explanation.definitionFit: This US Army post in Kentucky, home of the gold vault, is a military reservation.

clue.text: One related to 'Ol' Man River' — it's a grower

parts.note: Ma is the wife of the old man, a relative of his
the Tweed is a river on the English–Scottish border

explanation.surface: A song reference: someone connected to 'Ol' Man River' is a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ol' Man River' wants to be read as one song title; split it so 'Ol' Man' is the husband (Ma is related to him) and River is the Tweed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coarse grass growing on moors and dunes, so a plant that grows.

clue.text: Polynesians peeled bananas to be served with onions

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
peeling removes the outer skin, so the first and last letters go

explanation.surface: Islanders peeling bananas to serve alongside onions.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary term describes food cooked or served with onions, Lyon-style.

clue.text: Choose new bracelet, not needing female support

indicators.note: new letters are a fresh arrangement of the old
not needing means the piece is left out

parts.note: a bra is a woman's support garment

explanation.surface: Picking a new bracelet without needing any female support.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect is to choose, as by vote.

clue.text: To find fault, get in tradesman

parts.note: to carp is to complain or find fault
to enter is to get in

explanation.surface: Someone calls in a tradesman just to complain about the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker who builds and repairs timber structures is a tradesman.

clue.text: The less obvious code with letters cycled

indicators.note: a letter is moved from one end of the word round to the other

parts.note: an ethos is a code of values

explanation.surface: A puzzle note: a less obvious code is made by rotating letters.
explanation.walkthrough: ETHOS with its E moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The demonstrative for things further off, as against these near at hand, points at the less evident ones.

clue.text: At which point should I stop wild hyenas biting wife?

definitions.text: At which point should I stop

indicators.note: the anagram bites the other piece, holding it in its jaws
wild letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pourer's question, interrupted by hyenas savaging someone's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns HYENAS into SAYHEN, and W goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what a host invites a guest to say when enough drink has been poured.

clue.text: Number look around fish store

indicators.note: turned around means read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: An angler counts while looking around a fish shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler keeps caught fish alive in this net in the water.

clue.text: Young soldiers losing track

indicators.note: losing means a piece is taken away

parts.note: infantry are foot soldiers
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Young soldiers lose their way on the trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young child is the young of humankind.

clue.text: Row around a boat, just beginning to crack up

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a fallout is a quarrel or row

indicators.note: only the beginning, the first letter, is taken

explanation.surface: An argument around a boat that is starting to split apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is the quarrel, not oars; FALLOUT goes around A + B.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up and to collapse with laughter are idioms for helpless amusement.

clue.text: Playing with Tom Jones, say, not for all to see

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out

parts.note: Fielding's Tom Jones is a foundling, an abandoned baby
U is the British film rating for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Playing with the singer Tom Jones, something not fit for public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom Jones' suggests the singer; it is Fielding's novel hero, found as a baby. U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all.
explanation.definitionFit: To fondle is to caress or touch lovingly, playing with something by hand.

clue.text: Joyful, delighted and delirious to release hit novel

indicators.note: delirious letters are in wild disorder, a sign of rearrangement
releasing the hit lets those three letters go from the rearranged pool
novel means new, so the remaining letters form a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Joyful, delighted and wild with excitement as a novel becomes a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delirious' and 'novel' rearrange DELIGHTED AND, and 'to release' lets the letters of HIT go from it, leaving the nine letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Made glad describes someone who has become happy and cheered.

clue.text: Secure both sides on fire guards

indicators.note: the outer piece guards the inner one, surrounding it

parts.note: alight means burning, on fire
L and R stand for left and right, the two sides

explanation.surface: Fire guards placed on both sides keep something safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe and well, unharmed: one is secure and in no danger.

clue.text: Foolish European to carry around placard in Revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are read backwards
one piece is put around another

parts.note: to lug is to carry something heavy
a bill is a poster or placard

explanation.surface: A European protester carrying a placard during a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' looks like the uprising in the surface picture; here 'in Revolution' turns the whole assembly back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily duped and credulous, someone like that acts foolishly.

clue.text: Knight in chivalrous tale supports island race

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece supports the one above
one piece goes in another

parts.note: a roman is a medieval tale of chivalry, a romance
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight in a tale of chivalry backs an island race.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-distance triathlon of swimming, cycling and running is a gruelling race.

clue.text: Poorest area of best-loved city

parts.note: fave is informal for favourite, best-loved
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: The poorest area of everyone's favourite city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian shantytown is the poorest district of a city.

clue.text: After introduction to accountant, strapped son is rich

indicators.note: the introduction is the opening letter

parts.note: bound means tied up or strapped

explanation.surface: A son, strapped for cash, sees an accountant and finds he is rich after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strapped' suggests short of cash; here it means tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that abounds is plentiful, so a place teeming with it is rich in it.

clue.text: Anger aged female on purpose

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece goes on top of the next

parts.note: of can mean aged, as in a child of ten
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is angered deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to upset or anger them.

clue.text: Demand, without regret, cruel foreigner's love

indicators.note: without means the piece is taken out

parts.note: rue means regret
amour is French for love

explanation.surface: A cruel foreign lover demands love without regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public outcry is an insistent demand.

clue.text: Examined the fourth victim?

parts.note: a case is a patient or victim of illness
D is the fourth letter, as in case A, B, C, D

explanation.surface: A detective asks if the fourth victim has been looked at.
explanation.walkthrough: Cases are often labelled A, B, C, D, so the fourth victim is case D.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminals case a place when they examine it before a robbery.

clue.text: Split trousers pop damaged were useless

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so one piece pockets the other

parts.note: split is slang for leave quickly, fled

indicators.note: damaged letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Split trousers made pop music go wrong, a fashion failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb here; FLED pockets OPP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that flopped failed, proving useless.

clue.text: One poor parking place

parts.note: a role is a place or position

explanation.surface: A poor person's parking spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for proletarian, it is a working-class person, someone poor.

clue.text: Spoils brought back with mass offensive

indicators.note: brought back means read backwards

parts.note: rots means spoils or decays

explanation.surface: War spoils brought home after a massive offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like plunder; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm is a military assault, an offensive on a position.

clue.text: Common musical instrument for newbie

parts.note: a green is a village common
a horn is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A shared musical instrument for a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: An inexperienced newcomer is a novice or beginner.

clue.text: Went off semi-detached, well-known retreat

indicators.note: retreating goes backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
semi means half, so only the first half is used

parts.note: noted means famous, well-known

explanation.surface: A semi-detached house is a well-known retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-' keeps DETA; DETA + NOTED is then turned back by 'retreat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb that exploded went off.

clue.text: Not completely secure place

indicators.note: not completely means the last letter is cut

parts.note: steady means firm, secure

explanation.surface: A place that is not entirely safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In someone's stead means in their place.
